title: Binary Shock — PSR B1259−63 prototype
classification: Scientific visualization derived from an analytic axisymmetric model

reference_geometry.classification: direct model geometry and coordinate annotations

coordinate_axes.meaning: Cartesian axes of the exported IBSEn scene

disk_normal.meaning: Normal to the Be-star decretion-disk midplane

line_of_sight.meaning: Line-of-sight direction used by IBSEn for viewing-angle dependent calculations

reference_geometry.vector_display_note: Arrow lengths are viewer scales; only their origins and directions carry model meaning

apex.meaning: Analytic intrabinary-shock stagnation point where the opposing pressures balance on the symmetry axis

barycenter.source: origin of the IBSEn barycentric coordinate frame
barycenter.meaning: Center of mass of the binary system

orbit_display.coordinate_frame: Native IBSEn barycentric frame scaled by the instantaneous star-pulsar separation

unconstrained_choices.spin_axis_sky_position_angle: Not measured; placed in the line-of-sight/orbital-normal plane to minimize spin–orbit misalignment
unconstrained_choices.rotational_phase: Frozen at the closest magnetic-axis passage to the model line of sight
unconstrained_choices.sheet_shape: Parallel translucent laminae are an artistic depiction of a radio lighthouse beam, not an IBSEn-calculated emissivity volume

visual_geometry.palette: cyan with a near-white cyan core and longitudinal brightness striations
visual_geometry.endpoint: Placed far outside the binary framing so the beam crosses the viewport without a visible terminal cap
visual_geometry.scale_note: Length and width are artistic display scales and do not encode a calculated radio-emission distance or opening angle

decretion_disk.velocity_model: Keplerian rotation in the disk plane

pressure_balance_reference.classification: viewer reference tied to analytic pressure balance
pressure_balance_reference.representation_note: Both reference surfaces extend from their source body to the analytic apex. The Be-side sphere is a geometric extent reference, not an exact isosurface of the anisotropic summed external field; disk pressure is displayed separately

shock_surface.color_field: Doppler factor toward the IBSEn line of sight

visual_interpretation.shock_alpha: Display mapping derived from normalized Doppler factor; not physical opacity
visual_interpretation.body_lighting: Low-intensity browser point lights are artistic visibility cues; no extended stellar or pulsar halo is exported; the browser adds only a compact, smoothly fading white glow around the pulsar surface
visual_interpretation.pulsar_scale: Strongly enlarged; a physical neutron-star radius is unresolved at this scale
visual_interpretation.pulsar_surface_texture: Original artistic thermal-emissivity texture with subtle cool mottling and a few sparse low-emissivity spots; not an observed surface map or an IBSEn output
visual_interpretation.pulsar_radio_beam: Optional antipodal radio-beam layer aligned with a model-informed magnetic axis. Its orientation uses the IBSEn line of sight and published radio-polarization angles; its laminar sheet geometry, unmeasured sky azimuth, and frozen rotational phase are documented visual choices
visual_interpretation.star_orbit: Model-derived barycentric path in the native IBSEn coordinate frame
visual_interpretation.pulsar_orbit: Model-derived barycentric path shown in the same native frame and physical scale as the Be-star orbit
visual_interpretation.pressure_fields: The paper preset uses two geometric pressure-balance reference surfaces that reach the analytic apex and displays decretion-disk pressure as a separate volume; surface opacity is a display choice
visual_interpretation.disk_geometry: Diffuse browser volume sampled from the IBSEn radial pressure and vertical scale-height laws; no hard disk surface is stored in the GLB
visual_interpretation.disk_extent: IBSEn supplies no hard outer edge; the display radius is 1.35 times the pulsar's projected disk-plane radius and fades smoothly at the edge
visual_interpretation.turbulence: None added; the exported shock retains the axisymmetric IBSEn geometry
